note: Bifid uvula is a hallmark triad feature of Loeys-Dietz syndrome spectrum including SMAD2-related LDS6, though exact cohort frequencies remain to be definitively compiled across reported series.

evidence.text: Loeys-Dietz syndrome typically presents with aortic aneurysms, arterial tortuosity, hypertelorism, and bifid/broad uvula or cleft palate, with SMAD2 and SMAD3 confirmed as intracellular downstream effectors involved in the disease spectrum.

source.title: A mutation update on the LDS‐associated genes TGFB2/3 and SMAD2/3
source.quote: Most typically, LDS patients present with aortic aneurysms and arterial tortuosity, hypertelorism, and bifid/broad uvula or cleft palate.

evidence.text: SMAD2-positive cases exhibit typical Loeys-Dietz syndrome features such as cleft palate and bifid uvula, though mutation-positive cohorts remain relatively small.
